AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Atlanto-occipital rotatory dislocation (AORD) has been rarely reported in the literature; for this reason, the clinical-radiological characteristics of this injury are not well described.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The authors describe the case of a 67 years old male who sustained a cervical spine trauma. He only referred neck pain and was neurologically intact. The CT scan showed a rotatory displacement of the atlanto-occipital joints (AOJs) associated with a widened condylar-C1 interval; in addition, the MRI revealed injuries to the stabilizing ligaments of this area. A systematic literature review was also performed to identify previous cases of patients with AORD.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The patient was treated with craniocervical fixation from occipital to C1 achieving a good outcome. The literature review yielded 9 cases of patients with AORD. In comparison to cases of patients with atlanto-occipital dislocation (AOD), patients with rotatory dislocations have less severe degree of displacement of the AOJs and better clinical outcome.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Compared to previously classified atlanto-occipital dislocations, atlanto-occipital rotatory dislocation is an independent and unique variation. AORD presents with different biomechanical, clinical-radiologic and prognostic characteristics that represents an important addition to the spectrum of AOD injuries.
